clue.text: Promise club sandwiches for invalid

indicators.note: a sandwich holds its filling between two slices, so one word goes inside the other

parts.note: Spurs is the nickname of Tottenham Hotspur football club
an IOU is a written promise to pay

explanation.surface: A member of a club is excused because of a promise made on behalf of a sick person.
explanation.walkthrough: Spurs is the nickname of Tottenham Hotspur, a London football club. 'Invalid' looks like the noun for a sick person; it is the adjective meaning not valid.
explanation.definitionFit: Something spurious is false or not genuine, so it lacks validity in the same way an invalid claim does.

clue.text: Pea reportedly stuck up your nose

indicators.note: reportedly means as it is heard said, so the vegetable's name is taken by its sound

parts.note: the vegetable sounds like the name of the sixteenth letter

indicators.note: in a down clue, stuck up means pushed upwards, so the abbreviation is read from bottom to top

parts.note: YR is the standard abbreviation for your

explanation.surface: A child has pushed a pea up their nose.
explanation.walkthrough: P is followed by YR turned upwards, giving PRY. 'Nose' looks like a noun in the surface but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To nose about is to snoop inquisitively into other people's business, which is exactly what prying means.

clue.text: Paper clips left in field

indicators.note: a clip grips something within it, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: a ream is a standard quantity of paper, 500 sheets
L is the usual abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: Someone has dropped paper clips in a field and left them there.
explanation.definitionFit: A field of study or activity is a sphere or domain, which is the figurative sense of realm.

clue.text: Making mountains out of molehills at last, after senior ego bruised

indicators.note: after says the single letter is placed behind the reworked letters, not in front of them
something bruised has been battered out of shape, so these letters are knocked into a new order

parts.note: the letters of these two words are the raw material to be rearranged

indicators.note: at last points to the final letter of the word before it

parts.note: the final letter of molehills

explanation.surface: A self-important elder takes offence and makes mountains out of molehills.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface borrows the idiom for exaggerating trifles; read literally, 'Making mountains' is the definition of the geological term.
explanation.definitionFit: Orogenesis is the geological process by which crustal folding and uplift form ranges of high peaks.

clue.text: Element of blame attached to Head of Security

indicators.note: attached to says the two pieces are joined end to end
the head of a word is its first letter

parts.note: the first letter of Security
odium is general disapproval and blame directed at someone

explanation.surface: Part of the blame for a breach falls on the head of security.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Element of blame' reads as a share of the blame, but 'Element' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Sodium is a chemical element, the soft reactive metal with symbol Na.

clue.text: Put on muscle intermittently, for instance

parts.note: to put on weight is to add it

indicators.note: intermittently means on and off, so only every other letter is kept

parts.note: the second, fourth and sixth letters of muscle

explanation.surface: Bodybuilding advice: put on muscle in bursts, for example.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For instance' looks like a stock phrase; here 'instance' is a verb, to cite as an example, and 'for' links it.
explanation.definitionFit: To instance something is to cite it as evidence or example, which is what adducing means.

clue.text: Like starting the day naked

indicators.note: naked means stripped of its covering, so the outside letters are removed

parts.note: waking is what you do when the day begins

explanation.surface: Someone likes to start each day without clothes on.
explanation.walkthrough: WAKING loses its first and last letters to leave AKIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Akin means similar or related, the same as being like something else.

clue.text: Nameless hereditary halfwit raised for life of luxury

indicators.note: in a down clue, raised means lifted upwards, so the combined letters are read bottom to top
nameless means without a name, so the abbreviation for name is dropped

parts.note: native qualities are inborn, inherited rather than learned
a clod is a dull, stupid person

explanation.surface: An anonymous heir of limited intelligence is brought up to a life of luxury.
explanation.walkthrough: NATIVE without N, then CLOD, all turned upwards gives DOLCE VITA, Italian for 'sweet life'.
explanation.definitionFit: La dolce vita, Italian for the sweet life, is a phrase for indulgent, pleasure-seeking existence.

clue.text: Place to sell clobber close to a bar

indicators.note: to clobber is to hit hard, so these words are battered into a new order

parts.note: the letters of these words are the raw material to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Where to sell secondhand clothes, near a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clobber' looks like British slang for clothes, the stuff sold; it is the verb meaning bash. A car boot sale is a British market where people sell junk from their car boots (trunks).
explanation.definitionFit: A car boot sale is an outdoor gathering where private people sell secondhand goods from their vehicles.

clue.text: Bundle of energy going round in so many directions

indicators.note: going round means turning about, so the letters are read backwards
in says the letters sit inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the word boundaries of this phrase

explanation.surface: An energetic person rushing about in all directions.
explanation.definitionFit: A dynamo is figuratively a tirelessly energetic, forceful person, as well as a generator.

clue.text: Less healthy, surrounded by doctors and dentists?

definitions.note: the question mark flags a definition by example: dentists use drills

indicators.note: surrounded by says one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: Dr is the abbreviation for doctor, so DRS for several
the comparative of ill

explanation.surface: Sicker people are surrounded by medical professionals.
explanation.definitionFit: Dentists bore into teeth with a drill, so they can whimsically be called people who drill.

clue.text: Invented top cycling trick

indicators.note: cycling means going round, so the end letter is moved round to the front

parts.note: to trump someone is to beat or top them
to dupe someone is to trick them

explanation.surface: Someone has made up a clever stunt on a bicycle.
explanation.walkthrough: DUPE with its last letter rotated to the front gives EDUP.
explanation.definitionFit: A trumped-up charge is fabricated, made up falsely, so it has been invented.

clue.text: Engineering dons retire with a purpose in life

indicators.note: engineering means constructing or contriving, so these letters are built into a new order

parts.note: the letters of these words are raw material
taken as written

explanation.surface: University engineering lecturers retire with a sense of purpose.
explanation.definitionFit: Raison d'être is French for reason for existing, the thing that gives someone's existence its point.

clue.text: Singer of note in audition
Generational anxiety abruptly returns

indicators.note: abruptly means cut short, so the word loses its final letter

parts.note: a boomer is a member of the baby-boom generation
angst is a feeling of dread or anxiety

explanation.surface: Worry about generational divides suddenly comes back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Returns' looks like a noun; it is the verb, and 'Generational' must be read as a label for one generation.
explanation.definitionFit: To boomerang is to come back to the starting point, like the curved throwing stick.

clue.text: Publishes single review of children's doctor

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: to review is to look back, so the name is read backwards

parts.note: Dr Seuss wrote famous children's books

explanation.surface: A newspaper prints a lone review of a children's author's work.
explanation.definitionFit: To issue a book or magazine is to put it out to the public, the same as publishing it.

clue.text: Row and fight after firstly pre-recording what's on telly

definitions.note: a cryptic hint: the box once sat on top of the television

indicators.note: after places the pieces that follow it later in the answer

parts.note: a set-to is a brief quarrel or fight

indicators.note: firstly points to the opening letter of the word that follows

parts.note: the first letter of pre-recording
to box is to fight with fists

explanation.surface: An argument breaks out over recording a TV programme in advance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'What's on telly' reads as the programmes; here it is the device sitting on top of the set. Telly is British for television.
explanation.definitionFit: A set-top box is a decoder unit that traditionally sat on top of the television, as the name says.

clue.text: In favour of international European currency

parts.note: to be for something is to favour it
INT is a standard abbreviation for international

explanation.surface: Someone supports a single international currency for Europe.
explanation.definitionFit: The forint is the monetary unit of Hungary, which has not adopted the euro.

clue.text: Get sloshed in boat

indicators.note: sloshed means drunk, and a drunk's words come out jumbled

parts.note: the letters of these words are raw material

explanation.surface: An instruction to get drunk on a boat.
explanation.definitionFit: To obtain something is to acquire it or come to possess it, which is to get it.

clue.text: Antelope mainly run through area

indicators.note: mainly means for the most part, so all but the last letter is kept

parts.note: to impale is to run a spike or blade through
A is the abbreviation for area

explanation.surface: An antelope chiefly runs across a stretch of land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Run through area' looks like running across ground; 'run through' is to pierce with a spike.
explanation.definitionFit: The impala is a graceful reddish-brown antelope of southern and eastern African savannah.

clue.text: Women's personal success

parts.note: W is the abbreviation for women, as on toilet doors
inner feelings are private and personal

explanation.surface: A woman's private triumph.
explanation.definitionFit: A winner is something that succeeds, so a successful product or idea is called a winner.

clue.text: Fixed expression of disdain regularly suppressed, by order

indicators.note: every other letter is regularly held down, leaving only the alternate ones

parts.note: the second, fourth and sixth letters of disdain
the Order of Merit, abbreviated OM

explanation.surface: An official ordered to hold back their looks of contempt.
explanation.walkthrough: The Order of Merit is a British honour, so 'order' gives OM.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom is a set phrase whose wording is fixed and whose meaning is not literal.

clue.text: Actively desires to clothe backs of young waifs and strays

indicators.note: actively means busily in motion, so these letters are set moving into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram material

indicators.note: the back of a word is its last letter

parts.note: the final letters of young and waifs

explanation.surface: A charity is keen to dress homeless children and lost animals.
explanation.walkthrough: The two end letters join the seven of desires and all nine are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: To digress is to wander from the main subject, which is to stray off the point.

clue.text: Threw punch, catching end of chin

indicators.note: catching means grabbing and holding, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: to slug is to hit hard with the fist

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter

parts.note: the final letter of chin

explanation.surface: A boxer threw a punch that caught the opponent on the chin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Punch' looks like the blow thrown; it is the verb slug, holding N.
explanation.definitionFit: To sling is to throw something casually, so slung is its past tense, meaning threw.

clue.text: Shy drunk knocked back squash, not Scotch

indicators.note: knocked back means pushed backwards, so the word is read in reverse

parts.note: a sot is a habitual drunkard

indicators.note: not says the second word is taken away from the first

parts.note: taken as written
to scotch a rumour is to quash it

explanation.surface: A timid drinker downs a squash rather than whisky.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Knocked back' and 'Scotch' both suggest drinking; Scotch is the verb meaning put an end to. Squash is a British fruit cordial.
explanation.definitionFit: To shy is to throw something, as at a coconut shy, so it means the same as toss.

clue.text: Firm objections retrospectively dropped

indicators.note: retrospectively means looking back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: ifs and buts are objections
an animal's young are dropped when born

explanation.surface: A company's earlier objections have been withdrawn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Firm' looks like a company noun; it is the adjective meaning unyielding.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone firm in their views will not be moved, which is to be stubborn or obstinate.

clue.text: Tiny thing, uncharged, spending time in cell

indicators.note: spending time means using it up, so the abbreviation for time is lost

parts.note: the neutron is a subatomic particle with no electric charge
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A small, innocent person has been doing time behind bars without charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cell' and 'uncharged' suggest a prisoner held without charge; the particle loses its T.
explanation.definitionFit: A neuron is a nerve cell, the basic unit that carries signals in the nervous system.

clue.text: Old setters are in debt

parts.note: O is the abbreviation for old
a crossword setter calls themself me, so several setters are we

explanation.surface: Veteran puzzle compilers are short of money.
explanation.definitionFit: To owe money is to be under an obligation to repay it, which is being in debt.

clue.text: Ancient king reproduces without love

indicators.note: without means lacking, so the letter for love is taken out

parts.note: to xerox is to photocopy, reproducing a document
love is zero in tennis, shaped like O

explanation.surface: An old monarch has children without any affection.
explanation.definitionFit: Xerxes the Great was a fifth-century BC king of the Persian Achaemenid empire.

clue.text: Patient is gender-fluid

indicators.note: fluid means flowing and changeable, so the letters shift into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram material

explanation.surface: A patient in hospital is described as gender-fluid.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'is' that seems a link is part of the fodder too.
explanation.definitionFit: A resigned person accepts what happens without complaint, which is the same as bearing it patiently.
